Applications/Priming-and-SOC-Interaction.title: Priming and SOC Interactions
Applications/Priming-and-SOC-Interaction.content:
Priming and SOC Interactions
How biochar additions affect native soil organic carbon (SOC) mineralization (priming) and related CO₂ fluxes—distinct from the persistence of biochar’s own carbon (Permanence). Hub: GHG Fluxes. Sisters: Nitrous Oxide Fluxes, Methane Fluxes. Biology companion: Biochar Microbes and Soil Biology.
Report context: 2026-09-16.

1. Definitions






























TermMeaningURLPositive primingBiochar addition speeds mineralization of native SOC (more CO₂ from soil C)Framing in Zimmerman et al. 2011 doi.org/10.1016/j.soilbio.2011.02.005Negative primingBiochar addition slows native SOC mineralizationWang et al. 2016 doi.org/10.1111/gcbb.12266Labile C priming potentialFresh biochar’s easily mineralizable fraction can stimulate microbesCross & Sohi 2011 doi.org/10.1016/j.soilbio.2011.06.016Biochar’s own decompositionSeparate from priming—two-pool story in Wang 2016doi.org/10.1111/gcbb.12266 · Wang et al. 2016

2. Wang et al. 2016 meta-analysis (core)
Wang, Xiong & Kuzyakov (2016), GCB Bioenergy (DOI · Wang et al. 2016):
Biochar C decomposition (isotope studies)




















PoolShareMean residenceLabile~3%~108 daysRecalcitrant~97%~556 years
Dataset: 128 observations from 24 ¹³C/¹⁴C studies.
Priming of native SOC





















ResultValueOverall meanSOC mineralization −3.8% (95% CI −8.1% to +0.8%) — slight slowdown; CI includes zeroSignificant negative primingStudies <6 months: −8.6%; crop-derived biochar −20.3%; fast pyrolysis −18.9%; lowest pyrolysis T −18.5%; small application amounts −11.9%Positive primingSandy soils: +20.8%
Correction note (vault history): earlier drafts wrongly cited Wang 2016 for “short-term positive priming is common.” Short studies showed significant negative priming; positive priming was the sandy-soil subgroup (Key Sources corrections table).

3. Decade-scale field evidence
Weng et al. (2017) document decade-scale negative priming / SOC accrual under biochar, including stabilization of rhizodeposits (DOI).
Zimmerman et al. (2011) explore positive and negative priming among biochar-amended soils (DOI). Cross & Sohi (2011) link priming potential to labile C contents (DOI).

4. Jia et al. 2023 CO₂ / soil C pool
Jia et al. (2023) (DOI · Jia et al. 2023):

CO₂ emissions +7.4% overall; increase mainly from incubation and pot experiments—not significant in field studies
Soil carbon pool +38.1% upland, +33.4% paddy (includes biochar C contribution—read paper boundaries)
Combined GWP −7.7%; GHG intensity −14.3%


5. Inventory treatment (Woolf 2021)
Woolf et al. (2021) do not credit priming of native soil carbon because net negative priming was not statistically significant in the metas they rely on; method applies to mineral soils only—not organic soils (Histosols) or forest soils with an organic horizon, where positive priming is possible (DOI · Woolf et al. 2021).

6. Practice implications

Applications/Real-World-Soil-Projects.title: Real World Soil Projects
Applications/Real-World-Soil-Projects.content:
Real World Soil Projects
Named current or recent soil / agriculture deployments with outbound URLs. Only projects with verifiable primary or high-quality secondary sources are listed. Marketing claims without documentation are omitted. Companion: Soil and Agriculture · Crop Yield Effects · Biochar Compost and Manure Blends.
Report date: 2026-09-14.
Carbon-credit projects with verified soil end-use
Exomad Green — Concepción / Riberalta, Bolivia (Puro.earth)

Registry: Puro facility page states CORC 100+ durability; biochar from sawmill hardwood residues pyrolyzed ~600 °C; biochar donated to local Indigenous communities for agricultural soil enhancement (Puro — Exomad Green, Concepción).
Issuance (facility table on Puro page): 2023 21,252; 2024 58,344; 2025 102,458; 2026 91,457 CORCs (as published on page at fetch time).
Ag guidance: mix with inoculant; site-specific rates; planting-row / volume-% examples (Exomad biochar).
Field study (company report with CIAT; press 2025-07-04): Santa Cruz trials, 4 t ha⁻¹ once — corn +15% (up to +32% with fertilizer + microbes); beans +13% (up to +25%) (PDF; Bioenergy International). Yield ANOVA not significant and no fertilizer-only control — see Exomad Green Corn and Bean Field Study.
MRV partner case study: Carbonfuture — Exomad.

Verification note: Soil end-use is explicit on Puro and company pages (donation / farm application)—not a non-soil-only sink.
Charm Range & Plains Biochar — USA (Isometric)

Registry project: Charm co-produces bio-oil and biochar (Fort Lupton, CO) from wildfire-mitigation woody biomass; “We transport biochar via truck to various sites where it is sequestered via land application” (Isometric project).
Crediting period 01 Mar 2024 – 01 Mar 2029; issued volume shown on registry page; storage-site locations reported as secured upon offtake execution.
Company narrative: partners with farmers for water-stressed soils / productivity co-benefits; first Isometric CCP-labeled biochar credits (Charm blog).
Soil storage module reference: registry.isometric.com/module/biochar-storage-soil-environments/1.3

Verra Project 4679 — “Reignite,” Odisha, India (VM0044)

First project registered under VM0044 (announced 8 Oct 2024).
Rural farmers convert agricultural waste (instead of open burning) to biochar used on the same farms as a soil amendment (Verra news).
Methodology page: verra.org/methodologies/vm0044-biochar-utilization-in-soil-and-non-soil-applications-v1-2/

Commercial farms / vineyards (US)
Oasis Vineyard Trial — Monterey County, California

Partners: Sonoma Ecology Center, UC Riverside, Monterey Pacific Inc., Pacific Biochar; funded via California Department of Water Resources.
Pre-plant (2016–2017): biochar 10 t/ac, compost 15 t/ac, combo, vs control on sandy low-OM soils; incorporation ~30” in vine row.
Five harvests: combo +36%, biochar +25%, compost +29% average yield vs control; positive ROI by second harvest; incremental revenue by fifth harvest **9,752 / 12,569 / 14,937** per acre (biochar / compost / combo) at ~1,500/ton grapes; amendment costs (2016 delivered) biochar 240/ton**, compost **40/ton wet.
Primary source PDF: pacificbiochar.com/wp-content/uploads/Oasis-Vineyard-Trial_-5th-harvest_-Final-Draft_12.12.2023.pdf · Oasis Vineyard Trial 2023

Dominus Estate — Napa Valley, California

Pacific Biochar case study: 25 t/ac biochar cultivated to 36” on a 6-acre vineyard redevelopment after fallow; SOM-equivalent design discussion; earthworks fall/winter 2022, profile pit summer 2023.
URL: pacificbiochar.com/case-study-biochar-application-with-dominus-estate-in-napa-valley-after-2-years-fallow/

Sonoma Ecology Center × Napa Recycling — American Canyon pyrolysis (startup 2025)

23 Mar 2025 startup of CAL FIRE / Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund–supported facility converting surplus urban woodchips (A Plus Tree feedstock) to biochar at Napa Recycling; plan to blend with Napa Recycling compost for farm/garden customers (Sonoma Biochar Initiative, 17 May 2025).
Related SEC biochar program pages: sonomaecologycenter.org/biochar/

Earth Foundries × Napa Recycling — composting with biochar

2023 project report: 10% (by volume) biochar addition to green/food-waste composting reduced VOCs 33%, accelerated curing, affected finished compost nutrient/salinity metrics (PDF · Earth Foundries Co-Composting Report 2023).

Wakefield BioChar — NRCS CPS 336 channel & paper-mill partnership

Company overview of NRCS Soil Amendment 336 applications and discounted pricing for qualifying producers: wakefieldbiochar.com/learning-center/nrcs-program-and-biochar-overview/
DS Smith Riceboro, GA paper-mill ash → Wakefield soil products; company cites ~2 tons/acre average farm spreading: wakefieldbiochar.com/learning-center/ds-smith-partners-with-wakefield-to-convert-paper-mill-waste-to-useful-biochar/

US programs / demos (practice standard)

NRCS CPS 336 national standard & FAQ (rates, scenarios, biosolids exclusion): www.nrcs.usda.gov/resources/guides-and-instructions/soil-carbon-amendment-ac-336-conservation-practice-standard · nrcs-prod.azureedge.us/sites/default/files/2026-04/soil-carbon-amendment-ac-336-faq.pdf · NRCS CPS 336 FAQ 2026
Producer funding explainer (American Farmland Trust / Farmland Info hosting USBI-style guide): farmlandinfo.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2023/12/biochar_funding_for_US_producers_quick_guide_.pdf
USBI: biochar-us.org/
Note: publicly cited acreage totals for national EQIP 336 adoption are sparse in primary USDA statistical releases as of this research pass—treat state office reports as the authority when citing acres.

International field deployments (documented)






























LocationWhatURLNepalUrine-enhanced / liquid-enriched biochar fertilizers; pumpkin trial + 21 multi-crop trialsdoi.org/10.3390/agriculture5030723 · Schmidt et al. 2015 · doi.org/10.1002/ldr.2761 · Schmidt et al. 2017Brazil (Seropédica)Biochar on degraded pastures; environmental + CBAdoi.org/10.1038/s41598-019-47647-xBolivia (Exomad)Industrial production + farm soil use + yield trialslinks above · Exomad Green Corn and Bean Field StudyIndia (Odisha, Verra 4679)Farm-waste biochar returned to farmsverra.org/verra-registers-first-biochar-project/
Australian mine-spoil and pasture trials exist in the peer-reviewed literature (e.g., acacia–biochar mine rehab DOI); treat as research deployments unless a named commercial operator page is added later.
How to read these cases

Credit project ≠ agronomic trial. Exomad/Charm/Verra prove soil sink pathways under MRV; yield numbers need separate trial reports.
Vineyard California cases are among the best public multi-year agronomic + economic datasets (Oasis PDF).
Composting co-benefits (VOC, curing) are facility metrics—do not equate to field N₂O (GHG Fluxes).
Always check feedstock (forest residue, urban wood, ag waste) against local residue-retention rules (NRCS CPS 336 and US Ag).

Applications/Soil-and-Agriculture.title: Soil and Agriculture
Applications/Soil-and-Agriculture.content:
Soil and Agriculture
Chapter-length map of biochar in farm and soil systems: how it changes soil, what yield and GHG metas say, how to apply it, named real-world deployments, products/practices, constraints, and links to Permanence, NRCS CPS 336 and US Ag, and carbon-market soil pathways.
Report context: 2026-09-16.
Purpose and scope
Most historical agronomy and a large share of voluntary biochar CDR still assume soil end-use. Outcomes are context-specific (texture, pH, climate, rate, feedstock/process, fertilizer regime). This note synthesizes primary metas, NRCS practice guidance, and named projects—not universal prescriptions.
Child / related notes

























































TopicNoteYield metas & field evidenceCrop Yield EffectsN₂O / CH₄ / priming (ag framing)GHG Fluxes · Nitrous Oxide Fluxes · Methane Fluxes · Priming and SOC InteractionsRates, incorporation, banding, NRCS scenariosApplication Rates and Methods · Field Rates by System · Incorporation Topdress Banding · Equipment and Timing · On-farm Trial DesignNamed farms, vineyards, credit projectsReal World Soil ProjectsCompost / manure / COMBI clusterBiochar Compost and Manure Blends · Co-composting Science · Farm Co-composting Practice · Compost Blend Safety · Matrix Pathways for CreditsInoculation / charging / BBFsBiochar Inoculation for FertilizerNutrients & fertilizer chemistryBiochar Nutrients and Fertilizer ChemistryMicrobes & soil biologyBiochar Microbes and Soil BiologyCost / benefit (sourced only)Agronomic Economics · Cost Components · Fertilizer DisplacementUS EQIP/CSP practiceNRCS CPS 336 and US AgPersistence of applied CPermanence · Permanence Science for CreditsContaminants / specsContaminants and Quality · Properties · Product Standards EBC IBI
1. Soil mechanisms
1.1 Water retention and physical structure
Meta-analyses generally show larger hydrological benefits in coarse-textured soils:

Omondi et al. (2016) quantified mean effects including available water capacity (AWC) +15.1%, porosity +8.4%, bulk density −7.6%, and saturated hydraulic conductivity +25.2% across compiled studies (DOI).
Razzaghi et al. (2020) systematic review/meta-analysis asks whether biochar improves water retention and finds texture- and rate-dependent gains (DOI).
Wei et al. (2023) (939 observations) report field capacity / AWC responses by texture: coarse FC +23.8% / AWC +25.6%; medium +5.0% / +20.9%; fine +7.2% / +11.5% (DOI).
Blanco-Canqui (2017) reviews physical-property pathways (bulk density, porosity, aggregation, hydraulics) as functions of rate, feedstock, and soil (DOI).

Practice implication: sandy / low-OM soils are the clearest hydrological use-case; fine clays may show smaller AWC gains for the same rate.
1.2 Nutrients, CEC, and liming / pH
Jeffery et al. (2011) interpreted stronger productivity responses in acidic (+14%) and coarse/medium soils as consistent with liming and water-holding mechanisms, plus improved nutrient availability (DOI). Jeffery et al. (2017) found mean tropical yield benefits (~+25%) versus little mean benefit in temperate systems, again consistent with acid / low-fertility soil chemistry (DOI).
USDA NRCS CPS 336 guidance (April 2026 FAQ) states biochar is usually alkaline and most useful as a liming agent on acid soils; on soils already pH > 7, check liming equivalency and add cautiously. The FAQ walks liming-offset arithmetic (e.g., 1 ton biochar/acre at 9% CaCO₃ liming equivalency offsets ~9% of a 1 ton lime recommendation) (NRCS FAQ PDF · NRCS CPS 336 FAQ 2026).
NRCS also flags electrical conductivity (EC) / salts: high-ash manure chars can raise salinity; wood chars are typically lower EC. Spec-sheet examples in the FAQ contrast high-C wood char (low EC) vs poultry-manure char (high EC, high P/K, high liming) (same FAQ).
CEC and nutrient sorption are feedstock- and aging-dependent; Lehmann et al. (2021) summarize nutrient and liming co-benefits in the broader CDR/agronomy framing (DOI). Fresh, uninoculated biochar can temporarily immobilize nutrients—NRCS explicitly warns that “fresh biochar … has a chance to reduce crop yields by binding and immobilizing nutrients” and recommends compost/manure charging (FAQ; national standard also: inoculate with compost, compost tea, or manure — CPS 336 2022 PDF · NRCS CPS 336 Standard 2022).
1.2b Inoculation, charging, and biochar-based fertilizers
Fresh biochar can temporarily immobilize nutrients; NRCS and USBI therefore treat inoculation/charging as standard practice before agronomic use (NRCS FAQ; USBI Ag Guidelines · USBI Ag Guidelines 2023; CPS 336 inoculate clause: 2022 PDF).
Three modes (full chapter Biochar Inoculation for Fertilizer):

Nutrient charging — soak/impregnate with NPK solutions, urine, digestate, or manufacture BBFs (pre/post-pyrolysis). Melo et al. (2022) meta: BBFs +10% productivity vs fertilized controls (DOI). Scoping review of enrichment methods: Ndoung 2021.
Microbial inoculation — compost tea, PGP/AMF/EM on char carriers; meta shows gains vs biochar alone but weak commercial-field consistency (DOI · Ross & Emery 2025). Habitat in raw field-aged char can be sparse (Quilliam 2013 · DOI).
Co-composting (COMBI) — organic coating + nitrate capture; Kammann et al. (2015) untreated BC ~60% of control biomass vs co-composted up to ~305% of control (DOI); coating chemistry (Hagemann 2017); COMBI review (Antonangelo 2021 · DOI).

Practice ranges (sourced): charge 1–3 weeks (USBI); co-compost roughly 5–15% biochar w/w early (Pacific white paper · Pacific Biochar Compost White Paper 2023; Antonangelo); enriched fertilizers can work at ≪2 t ha⁻¹ root-zone (Schmidt 2017 · DOI; urine protocol Schmidt 2015 · DOI).
Credit/MRV: Puro soil amendment pure/mixed (AF1–AF2) remains eligible end-use; co-composting does not erase aromatic C stability for permanence chemistry (Hagemann 2017; Puro Biochar Methodology Edition 2025). Details: Biochar Inoculation for Fertilizer §9.
1.2c Nutrients & fertilizer chemistry (chapter pointer)
Deep chemistry of N/P/K, CEC/AEC, liming, BBF formulations, and fertilizer-use efficiency: Biochar Nutrients and Fertilizer Chemistry. Headline metas: soil inorganic N mean ~−11% NH₄⁺ / −10% NO₃⁻ in the first year class of evidence (Nguyen 2017); BBFs at mean 0.9 t ha⁻¹ give +10% productivity vs fertilized controls (Melo 2022); biochar+fertilizer field synergy ~+15% (Ye 2020 · PDF).
1.2d Microbes & soil biology (chapter pointer)
Habitat vs sparse colonization, inocula efficacy, AMF/PGPR, priming, and disease-suppression uncertainty: Biochar Microbes and Soil Biology. Key contrast: biota review (Lehmann 2011) vs sparse field colonization of wood char (Quilliam 2013); inocula meta favors local/fungal over commercial products (DOI).
1.3 Microbial habitat and SOC interactions
Porous carbon provides habitat and alters redox / sorption environments that shape N cycling (see GHG Fluxes). For native soil organic carbon:

Wang et al. (2016) meta-analysis finds a slight, non-significant mean slowdown of SOC mineralization (−3.8%, 95% CI −8.1% to +0.8%), with significant negative priming in studies under six months (−8.6%) and positive priming in sandy soils (+20.8%) (DOI).
Weng et al. (2017) document decade-scale negative priming and SOC accrual under biochar in a field context (DOI).

NRCS positions biochar as long-lived SOM support versus compost’s shorter labile pulse: FAQ cites research that roughly 60–80% of biochar C can remain after 100 years versus 2–14% for compost C, and that ~10 yd³ biochar can match 1-year soil-C increase of ~40 yd³ compost in their comparison framing (FAQ). Cross-check permanence math with Permanence and Woolf et al. 2021 (DOI).
2. Crop / agronomic evidence (summary)
Full tables live in Crop Yield Effects. Headline metas:








































SourceYield / productivity findingURLJeffery et al. 2011Grand mean ~+10% (subgroup means −28% to +39%)doi.org/10.1016/j.agee.2011.08.015Jeffery et al. 2017Tropical mean ~+25%; temperate mean little/no benefitdoi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aa67bdYe et al. 2020Biochar + fertilizer ~+15% vs fertilizer alone in field setwww.css.cornell.edu/faculty/lehmann/publ/SoilUseManage%2036%2C%202-18%202020%20Ye.pdfJia et al. 2023Overall crop yield +9.4%doi.org/10.1002/ldr.4868Schmidt et al. 2015 (Nepal pumpkin)Large gains from urine-enhanced low-dose biochardoi.org/10.3390/agriculture5030723Pandit/Schmidt et al. (21 Nepal trials)Biochar-based fertilizers across 13 cropsdoi.org/10.1002/ldr.2761
Decision rule of thumb (evidence-based, not a guarantee): expect stronger agronomic ROI where soils are acidic, coarse, low-OM, tropical/subtropical, or degraded; temperate fertile systems often need compost/manure blends, banding, or CDR/policy payments to pencil (see Agronomic Economics, Jeffery 2017).
3. GHG fluxes from agricultural soils
Deep dive: GHG Fluxes · Nitrous Oxide Fluxes · Methane Fluxes · Priming and SOC Interactions. For farm planning:

N₂O: Cayuela et al. (2014) classic meta ~−54% across lab and field studies (DOI); Jia et al. (2023) ~−26.8% across incubation, pot and field studies (DOI). H:C_org of the char is a key moderator (Cayuela 2015).
CH₄: Mixed; Jia 2023 global mean −13.0%; paddies and flooded systems need site-specific reading (DOI). Woolf et al. (2021) inventory method assumes no net CH₄ change for simplicity (DOI).
Inventory conservatism: Woolf 2021 optional N₂O credit only for applications >10 Mg C ha⁻¹ in year 1 (illustrative −23%), and not for organic/forest soils (DOI).

CDR credit tonnage is dominated by stable biochar C, not annual N₂O co-benefits—see Biochar as Durable CDR, MRV Stack.
4. Application methods (pointer)
Full practice notes: Application Rates and Methods · Field Rates by System · Incorporation Topdress Banding · Equipment and Timing · On-farm Trial Design; blends: Biochar Compost and Manure Blends · Co-composting Science · Farm Co-composting Practice.

Research rates: often 5–50+ t ha⁻¹ (extremes to 100 t ha⁻¹ in Jeffery 2011) — not default farm advice (DOI).
Enriched fertilizers: agronomic doses can be <2 t ha⁻¹ when nutrient-loaded (Schmidt/Pandit line; DOI).
NRCS CPS 336 planning: FAQ — 4–10 cubic yards per acre is a good starting range; FY2024 100% biochar payment scenario assumes 4 yd³/ac; blend scenarios specify compost + biochar quantities (FAQ).
Incorporation: tillage, trenching, no-till drill/prills, manure injectors, fertigation of fines, permanent-bed mixing; surface-only on slopes risks wind/water loss (FAQ).
Pasture: CPS 336 allowed on pasture; not on native rangeland except facilitating Range Planting (550) or Critical Area Planting (342) (FAQ).

5. Real-world current applications (critical)
Named, sourced deployments are catalogued in Real World Soil Projects. Snapshot:

Credit stacking warning: NRCS EQIP/CSP payments for CPS 336 are not carbon credits. Coexistence with voluntary CDR requires contractual double-claim prevention — Double Counting and Credit Ownership, NRCS CPS 336 and US Ag.
6. Products and practice

Standards: Product Standards EBC IBI — EBC, IBI, NRCS Table 3 (H:C_org <0.7, C_org >10%) (CPS 336 PDF).
Enriched / biochar-based fertilizers: Schmidt/Pandit Nepal results show low-dose, nutrient-loaded chars can outperform bulk raw char (DOI).
Named commercial lines (sourced marketing pages, not endorsements): Wakefield Original / CarbonBoost / Pro Garden Mix (page); Pacific Biochar compost–biochar bulk blends (page); Napa Recycling compost + SEC biochar blend pathway (SBI).
US directories / tools: USBI, NRCS Soil Carbon Amendment tools / Biochar Atlas references on NRCS soil-carbon-amendments page.

7. Constraints — when it does not help (or hurts)























































RiskEvidence / guidanceURLTemperate fertile soils, weak mean yieldJeffery 2017doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aa67bdFresh uncharged char → N immobilizationNRCS FAQnrcs-prod.azureedge.us/sites/default/files/2026-04/soil-carbon-amendment-ac-336-faq.pdfHigh-EC manure chars → salinityNRCS FAQsameAlkaline soils + high-liming charNRCS FAQsameBiosolids chars / PFASExcluded under CPS 336same FAQContaminated feedstocks (PAHs, metals)Contaminants and Quality; Jeffery 2011 biosolids subgroup −28% yielddoi.org/10.1016/j.agee.2011.08.015Over-application cost without yieldGalinato et al. 2011 economics; Oasis costsdoi.org/10.1016/j.enpol.2011.07.035 · Oasis PDFSurface application on erodible slopesNRCS: do not apply where runoff/wind loss significantFAQResidue stripping for feedstockCPS 336: residues needed for soil cover / forest health not eligible feedstock pathFAQ
8. How soil use connects to permanence and credits

Produce & test to low H:C_org → Properties, Permanence.
Apply to eligible sink (soil / compost / etc.) with chain-of-custody → MRV Stack.
Choose methodology (soil modules differ): Verra VM0044, Puro Biochar Methodology Edition 2025, Isometric Biochar Protocol (soil storage module: registry.isometric.com/module/biochar-storage-soil-environments/1.3), CSI Global Biochar C-Sink.
Separate agronomic value (water, nutrients, yield) from credit value (durable C) in farm budgets → Agronomic Economics, Market Volumes and Pricing.

9. Decision tree (evidence-based)
Use this as a planning screen—not a substitute for soil tests or NRCS planners.

Soil screen — Prefer candidates with low OM, coarse texture, or acidic pH (Jeffery 2011/2017; NRCS FAQ). Skip or pilot carefully if alkaline, high-EC, or already high-P with manure-char products (Jeffery 2011; Jeffery 2017; FAQ).
Product screen — Spec sheet: C_org, H:C_org (<0.7 for CPS 336), ash, EC, liming equivalent, metals, PAHs as required by market/standard (Contaminants and Quality; CPS 336 PDF).
Rate screen — Start near NRCS 4–10 yd³/ac unless a vineyard redevelopment or research protocol justifies higher (Oasis 10 t/ac; Dominus 25 t/ac) (FAQ; Oasis; Dominus).
Blend screen — Default to compost/manure charge for agronomy; consider co-composting if a local facility pathway exists (Biochar Compost and Manure Blends).
Placement screen — Band/row for perennials and low doses; broadcast+incorporate for field crops; avoid unprotected surface on HEL slopes (FAQ).
Finance screen — Model yield-only, yield+EQIP, and yield+CDR cases separately (Agronomic Economics; Galinato 2011).
MRV screen — If selling removals: registry choice, application evidence, ownership, no double claim with CPS 336 (MRV Stack, Double Counting and Credit Ownership).

10. Feedstock × soil matching

Residue ethics: CPS 336 disallows paying for char made from residues that should stay for soil cover or forest health (FAQ). Production side: Feedstocks, Production Hub.
11. Monitoring for dual agronomy + credit use
Minimum practical stack (operator checklist also in NRCS CPS 336 and US Ag):

Batch IDs, weigh tickets, moisture, lab H:C_org / C_org
Geotagged application polygons and rates (yd³/ac or t/ha)
Incorporation depth / method notes
Baseline and follow-up soil tests (pH, OM, P, EC, bulk density if hydrology is a claim)
Yield records by treatment strip where claiming agronomic ROI
5+ year record retention common in credit MRV expectations (MRV Stack)
Contract language: who owns CORCs/VCUs vs NRCS payment beneficiary

Isometric soil storage module (example of soil-environment requirements): registry.isometric.com/module/biochar-storage-soil-environments/1.3
Puro biochar methodology edition cluster: Puro Biochar Methodology Edition 2025
Verra VM0044 (soil and non-soil): verra.org/methodologies/vm0044-biochar-utilization-in-soil-and-non-soil-applications-v1-2/
12. Open research gaps (do not invent answers)

National EQIP/CSP acreage statistics for CPS 336 by year/state (need USDA program reports)
Long-term (>10 yr) temperate row-crop yield meta limited to modern enriched products
Standardized farmgate price indexes for bulk agricultural biochar (distinct from CORC prices)
Head-to-head N₂O field campaigns at CPS 336–realistic rates (≪ Woolf’s 10 Mg C ha⁻¹ inventory threshold)

13. Deep dive — water, CEC, and liming numbers
Hydrology metas (copyable figures)





















































MetricMean effectConditionsDOI / URLAWC+15.1%Omondi et al. 2016 global meta meandoi.org/10.1016/j.geoderma.2016.03.029Porosity+8.4%samesameBulk density−7.6%samesameKsat+25.2%samesameFC / AWC coarse soils+23.8% / +25.6%Wei et al. 2023doi.org/10.1016/j.geoderma.2023.116591FC / AWC medium+5.0% / +20.9%Wei 2023sameFC / AWC fine+7.2% / +11.5%Wei 2023same
Systematic review companion: Razzaghi et al. 2020 (DOI). Narrative physical-property review: Blanco-Canqui 2017 (DOI).
Liming arithmetic (NRCS worked example)
If soil test calls for 1 ton lime/ac and producer applies 1 ton biochar/ac with liming equivalency 9% CaCO₃, remaining lime need ≈ 0.91 ton/ac (FAQ). Using biochar only as a lime substitute does not meet CPS 336’s stated purposes if that is the sole intent—the FAQ warns against treating liming-as-purpose as 336-eligible framing.
CEC / nutrient sponge
Biochar’s surface functional groups and porosity can increase effective nutrient retention, but fresh high-temperature wood chars may have relatively low CEC until oxidized/aged or compost-charged. Operational guidance therefore emphasizes inoculation (CPS 336 PDF). Lehmann et al. 2021 synthesize nutrient and liming co-benefits in the CDR context (DOI).
14. Glossary (soil/ag)

AWC — available water capacity (plant-available water between field capacity and permanent wilting point).
Charging / inoculation — loading biochar with nutrients and/or microbes (compost, manure, teas, fertilizers) before or during application.
CPS 336 — NRCS Conservation Practice Standard Soil Carbon Amendment.
H:C_org — molar hydrogen to organic carbon ratio; lower ⇒ more aromatic / persistent; NRCS max 0.7.
Liming equivalency — % CaCO₃ neutralizing value of the amendment.
Priming — change in mineralization rate of native SOC after amendment (positive = faster loss; negative = slower).
yd³/ac — cubic yards per acre (NRCS contracting unit); convert with measured bulk density.

Carbon-Markets/Biochar-as-Durable-CDR.title: Biochar as Durable CDR
Carbon-Markets/Biochar-as-Durable-CDR.content:
Biochar as Durable CDR
Core pathway

Photosynthetic capture — Biomass stores atmospheric CO₂ (~45–50% C dry matter, depending on feedstock).
Thermochemical conversion — Pyrolysis or gasification (typically >350 °C, limited/no O₂) converts a substantial fraction into an aromatic carbon matrix (biochar); gases/oils must be accounted for in LCA.
Durable storage — Soil application, burial, or materials (concrete, asphalt, composites) so that a large fraction of organic C does not return to the atmosphere on multi-decadal to millennial timescales.

This is carbon dioxide removal (CDR) / biochar carbon removal (BCR) when the credited outcome is net atmospheric CO₂ stored in a durable reservoir, after subtracting lifecycle emissions and counterfactual storage.
CDR vs avoidance
Avoidance / reduction claims (displacing fossil fuels with pyrolysis heat; avoiding methane from waste) are a different claim. Most modern biochar removal methodologies deliberately credit durable storage of biochar carbon, not fossil displacement. Mixing removal and avoidance without clear boundaries is a common greenwashing critique—see Risks and Controversies.
Why treated as durable

Higher pyrolysis severity → lower H/C_org (and often O/C_org) → slower mineralization.
IPCC 2019 · IPCC 2019 Biochar Appendix F_perm ≈ 0.65 / 0.80 / 0.89 by temperature class at ~20 °C baseline.
Woolf et al. (2021) refined with H/C_org + soil temperature. DOI: 10.1021/acs.est.1c02425
Petrographic approaches (Ro / inertinite) argue millennial persistence for highly condensed fractions (Sanei et al. 2024; DOI: 10.1016/j.coal.2023.104409).

Important: Standards do not typically credit 100% of biochar C—they apply permanence factors, LCA deductions, leakage, and (in some programs) mandatory offsetting of process emissions.
Soil / materials pathways
Dominant voluntary-market pathway for ag operators: soil application (direct spreading, compost/manure/digestate blends, or bedding/feed routes where allowed). Non-soil pathways (concrete, asphalt) also generate credits under Verra, Puro, Isometric, and CSI with different end-use evidence.

Carbon-Markets/Double-Counting-and-Credi.content:
Double Counting and Credit Ownership
Problem patterns

Same tonne, multiple claims — product “carbon footprint reduction,” voluntary credit, and compliance instrument simultaneously.
Value-chain ambiguity — grower, pyrolyzer, farmer, and credit buyer without clear ownership contracts. Isometric and CSI emphasize single credit owner + registry tracking.
Methodology overlap — soil-carbon farming methodologies and biochar CDR both claiming the same C.
Practice stacking — NRCS CPS 336 and US Ag cost-share payments coexist with voluntary CDR credits only if contracts prevent double claiming the same tonne.

Practical safeguards

Contractually assign who owns the climate claim before application
Retire unique registry tonnes; do not also market unretired “carbon-negative” product claims for the same mass
Disclose stacking of NRCS / other ag payments with credit issuance
Maintain chain-of-custody records (often ≥5 years)—see MRV Stack

MRV Stack
What is measured



































DomainTypical measurementsLab vs fieldFeedstockWaste/residue status, sustainability, counterfactual fate, transport, cultivation emissionsDocumentary + activity dataPyrolysisTemperature, residence time, O₂ exclusion, mass balance, energy use, flue-gas CH₄/N₂O/COContinuous sensors and/or periodic stack testsBiochar characterizationC_org, H/C_org, O/C_org, ash, moisture, metals, PAHs, PCDD/F, PCBs; optional Ro, HyPyAccredited lab (ISO 17025)Application / storageDry mass delivered & applied; GPS; incorporation; matrix mix ratios; custodyField / logistics evidencePermanenceModeled F_durable / GPC–SPC from lab properties ± soil TLab proxies + models
Why not field SOC stock change? Distinguishing biochar-C from native SOC at scale is difficult; standards credit characterized biochar applied to an eligible sink, discounted by permanence models—not measured ΔSOC.
Typical high-integrity characterization package

Proximate/ultimate: moisture, ash, VM, C/H/N/O/S
C_org (total C − inorganic C)
Molar H/C_org and O/C_org
Contaminants: Pb, Cd, Cu, Ni, Hg, Zn, Cr, As; PAHs; dioxins/furans; PCBs
Agronomic: pH, EC/salts, liming, nutrients
Advanced (program-dependent): Ro, BC_HyPy, Rock-Eval

Methods often cited: ASTM D5373 / D1762 / D4373; ISO 16948, 18134, 10390, 17025; ISO 7404-5 for Ro.
Common issuance pattern

Produce & characterize batch
Deduct LCA emissions (CSI: retire offsets from emission portfolio)
Prove eligible end use with custody trail
Apply permanence factor → issue credits ex post
Maintain records (often ≥5 years); monitor reversal risks

3. Why these buyers choose BCR
Synthesized from public statements collected in Snapshot 2025 (not invented):

Ready-now — shorter path from contract to delivery than many engineered peers (Market Volumes and Pricing).

Start-small optionality — trials under 100 t lower organizational barriers.
MRV / standard trust — Puro CORCs, Isometric modules, CCP labels, dMRV (Carbonfuture).
Co-benefits — soil, air quality, community, waste diversion (deal-specific).
Permanence framing — ≥100y / several centuries / 1000y depending on pathway (Durable CDR Quality Tiers · Permanence Science for Credits).

Nasdaq additionally frames purchases as supporting marketplace scale and UN SDG co-benefits (Snapshot).

Permanence science vs commercial tiers
Commercial durability claims map to science stacks:

Delivery quality (often under-weighted)

A Tier-A method with weak operational delivery underperforms a Tier-A method with proven tonnes—see delivery ratios in Market Volumes and Pricing and supplier track records in Supply Landscape.

Contextual notes on selected deals
Microsoft × Exomad Green (1.24 Mt)

Largest BCR agreement by volume at announcement (May 2025); among largest durable CDR deals generally (Exomad claim).
Builds on prior >32 kt relationship.
Biomass: forestry residues that would otherwise be open-burned; biochar to local agricultural soils.
Facilities: Concepción & Riberalta (expanded); third facility under construction at announcement time.
Exomad goal cited: 1 Mt CO₂ / yr by 2027 (Exomad May 2025).
Delivery share claim at announcement: 27% of durable CDR deliveries (CDR.fyi data cited by Exomad, Apr 2025 context).

Google × Varaha & Charm (100 kt each)

Google called them “the largest biochar carbon removal deals to date” as of 16 Jan 2025 (Google blog)—later surpassed by Microsoft–Exomad and Microsoft–Liferaft.
Adds biochar alongside EW, DAC, Frontier, and Symbiosis toolkit.

Google × AMP (200 kt)

MSW organics recovered via AI sortation → biochar; initial use as landfill daily cover.
Paired methane-framework work with Google.
SPSA Virginia 20-year processing contract is the underlying project infrastructure (AMP release).

Microsoft × Liferaft (1 Mt)

Largest US biochar offtake announced to date (coverage consensus; Liferaft primary emphasizes rural Midwest jobs + Microsoft carbon-negative goal).
Biochar–compost mix for approved agricultural end uses.
Second-largest BCR purchase historically per CDR.fyi Q1 2026 (~43.5% of that quarter’s contracted durable CDR).

Altitude × Empacar (>305 kt)

Financier procurement of CORCs (not necessarily end-corporate retirement at signing).
Bioflux cited as biochar program partner.
Positions Bolivia as multi-supplier BCR hub alongside Exomad.

Supercritical × Exomad (up to 500 kt)

Emphasizes near-term deliverable inventory vs long-dated promises.
Extends partnership; Supercritical previously facilitated >100 kt of Exomad credits.
Exomad claims >320 kt produced to date and >200% YoY production growth (Apr 2026 release).

Microsoft × Carba (44 kt)

Storage pathway: low-oxygen burial / landfill cover—not classic soil amendment.
First project on Isometric’s Biochar Storage in Low Oxygen Burial Environments module (CDR.fyi alert).
DOE Carbon Negative Shot Pilot grant ($7M) referenced in Carba release.

Market Volumes and Pricing
Chapter-length synthesis of biochar carbon removal (BCR) market volumes and price signals as of 2026-09-14. Figures are from primary / high-signal public sources only—chiefly CDR.fyi abridged reports and Puro × Nasdaq indexes. Do not treat this note as live market data; re-pull sources before diligence.
Related: Market Hub · Buyers and Offtakes · Historical Deals · Price Indexes and Benchmarks · Supply Landscape · Durable CDR Quality Tiers · Puro Pricing and CORC Indexes · Risks and Controversies

1. How to read the three volume metrics

























MetricWhat it measuresWhy it mattersContracted / purchasedForward offtakes + spot sales reported to trackersDemand & bankability; dominated by multi-year megadealsDeliveredTonnes actually issued / delivered ex-postOperational proof; BCR leads all durable CDR methods hereRetiredTonnes cancelled on a registry for a climate claimFinal use of the credit; liquidity + claim integrity
CDR.fyi tracks durable removals (hundreds to thousands of years permanence). Coverage claim in Q1 2026 notes: ~97%+ of publicly disclosed durable CDR contract volume (methodology caveats).

2. Cumulative BCR volumes (Q1 2022 → H1 2025)
Primary source: Biochar Carbon Removal Market Snapshot 2025 (published 2025-09-09).
Headline table




























































MetricFigureNotesCumulative BCR contracted3.04 MtQ1 2022 through end-H1 2025Of which H1 20251.6 MtExceeded all prior periods combined since 2022Cumulative delivered683 ktEnd-Q2 2025 (highlights also list 658 kt—prefer body 683 kt)Cumulative retired330 ktEnd-Q2 2025 (highlights also list 302 kt—prefer body 330 kt)Delivered : purchased~22% (1 : 4.5)Large forward books vs physical deliveryRetired : delivered~50% (1 : 2)Half of delivered tonnes retired by end-Q2 2025Unique BCR purchasers290~5× more buyers than next CDR method by buyer countAvg volume / purchaser / year542 t (2022) → 762 t (H1 2025)Rising average order sizeEx-Microsoft avg deal size197 t → 278 tStill small vs megadealsMedian contracted90 t (2024) → 73 t (2025 YTD in snapshot)Majority of purchasers still <100 t
Growth narrative

2022–2024: purchase tonnage roughly tripled year-over-year; 2024 purchases exceeded all prior years combined.
Q2 2025: largest BCR quarter ever, driven by Microsoft–Exomad Green ≥1.24 Mt (Exomad May 2025; Historical Deals).
Deliveries and retirements roughly doubled annually 2022–2024; Q1–Q2 2025 retirements were closer to flat vs year-ago quarters (+12% / +0.4%).

5. Price trends — index vs bilateral
5.1 Public index (Puro × Nasdaq)
Retrieved 2026-09-14 from Puro Carbon Removal Indexes:

Deep how-to-read: Price Indexes and Benchmarks · Puro Pricing and CORC Indexes.
CORCCHAR < CORCX in this snapshot: biochar trades at a discount to the all-CORC composite on reported near-term Puro transactions—not proof of a global BCR discount vs Verra/Isometric/CSI.
5.2 Survey / disclosed-order pricing (CDR.fyi)






























ObservationDetailCaveatAll-method WAP ↓490 → 320 / t (2023→2024) (YIR)Mix of DAC, BECCS, EW, BCR, etc.Biochar ↑+18% YoY (YIR)Exact BCR mean undisclosed in abridged YIRNarrow BCR bandYIR says biochar settled into a “relatively narrow price range”No numeric band published in abridged postMegadeal unit pricesGenerally not in press releasesMajor transparency gap
5.3 Index vs bilateral offtakes

























ChannelCharacteristicsIndex (CORCCHAR)Near-term reported CORC trades; transparent €/t level; Puro-onlySpot platform inventoryCertified tonnes; may track near indexMulti-year offtakesFirm + optional volumes; prices usually confidential; may embed delivery risk, co-benefits, dMRV requirementsIntermediated portfoliosSupercritical, Senken, Watershed, Patch, Carbonfuture, etc.; 74% of Q1 2026 tonnes
Science-side abatement cost ranges (e.g., literature ~$70–360/t) are not credit market prices—see Quantitative Benchmarks.
5.4 Quality-tier effects on price
Public abridged sources do not quantify CCP-label or 1000-year-path premiums in $/t. Practical segmentation hypotheses (unverified price deltas):

Buyers requiring CCP methodology labels today may prefer Verra VM0044 VCUs.
Buyers requiring 1000-year Ro / burial may prefer Isometric Biochar Protocol (e.g., Carba–Microsoft).
Buyers optimizing near-term delivery + CORCCHAR discovery may prefer Puro CORC200+ inventory.
Uncertified marketing claims should clear at zero credit value for neutralization accounting (Durable CDR Quality Tiers).


6. Liquidity & cycle time

























SignalFigureSourcePuro biochar CORC issuance → transfer/retirement95 days (2021) → 22 days (mid-2025)Snapshot 2025 citing Puro Aug 2025 reportRetired : delivered (BCR cumulative)~50% by end-Q2 2025Snapshot 2025Intermediary share of Q1 2026 tonnes74%Q1 2026
Faster CORC turnover improves working-capital dynamics for suppliers on the Puro stack (Puro Project Cycle and MRV · Puro Pricing and CORC Indexes).

7. Why buyers choose BCR (volume implications)
From Snapshot business-case synthesis (Swiss Re, SEB, Tide, Nasdaq, and diversified majors):

Rapid contracting → delivery relative to DAC/BECCS.
Lower prices relative to many engineered methods (qualitative; exact differentials sparse).
Ability to start small (<100 t trials) — explains 290 unique purchasers.

These structural advantages explain why BCR can be ~10% of contracted durable CDR yet ~86–92% of delivered/retired tonnes.

8. Gaps / what isn’t public

Unit prices on Microsoft–Exomad, Microsoft–Liferaft, Google–AMP, Altitude–Empacar, Supercritical–Exomad.
Full registry mix of delivered BCR (Puro vs Verra vs Isometric vs CSI) in abridged posts.
Post–Q1 2026 quarterly abridged update (none fetched as of 2026-09-14 beyond May 2026).

Price Indexes and Benchmarks
Public price discovery for biochar / engineered CDR is thin. The main open biochar-specific index is Puro × Nasdaq CORCCHAR. This note explains what it measures, how it relates to bilateral offtakes, and what remains opaque. Research retrieved 2026-09-14.
Deep Puro fee + index companion: Puro Pricing and CORC Indexes
Volume context: Market Volumes and Pricing · Historical Deals · Durable CDR Quality Tiers
Parent MOC: Market Hub

1. Live index pages (bookmark these)

2. CORCX and CORCCHAR — snapshot (as of retrieval)
Source: Puro Carbon Removal Indexes, retrieved 2026-09-14:





























IndexScopeAug 2026 level1-month change6-month changeYTD changeCORCXComposite of all CORC pathway transactions€150.40+€12.05 (+8.71%)+€10.29 (+7.35%)+€15.31 (+11.33%)CORCCHARBiochar CORC transactions only€135.35+€6.12 (+4.74%)+€3.81 (+2.74%)+€2.50 (+1.88%)
How to read them

Transaction-based: Indexes track reported near-term CORC transactions under a Nasdaq methodology—not a theoretical model price.
Puro-only: Levels apply to CORCs under the Puro Standard. They are not quotes for Verra Verra VM0044 VCUs, Isometric Biochar Protocol credits, or CSI Global Biochar C-Sink C-sinks.
Near-term bias: Designed for price discovery on inventory that trades soon—not a perfect proxy for 10-year offtake strike prices.
CORCCHAR vs CORCX: In Aug 2026, biochar sat ~€15 below the all-CORC composite. That gap can reflect pathway mix (other CORC methods in CORCX), liquidity, and timing—not a global “biochar discount” law.
EU benchmark caveats: Puro notes potential qualification as a benchmark under Regulation (EU) 2016/1011 for certain financial uses—read the factsheet before referencing in contracts.
More indexes planned as other methodologies gain transaction density (Puro page statement).

Full commercial context (fees, offtake waiver, liquidity days): Puro Pricing and CORC Indexes · Puro.earth Overview.

Practical rule: Use CORCCHAR for directional Puro biochar price discovery; use press releases + CDR.fyi for volumes; assume unknown strike prices on megadeals unless a party discloses them.

5. Quality-tier effects (unquantified)
Durable CDR Quality Tiers hypothesizes CCP / 1000-year / delivery premia. As of research date:

No public table of BCR $/t by registry or CCP label in CDR.fyi abridged posts.

Puro biochar methodology not yet CCP-Approved while program is CCP-Eligible (ICVCM 2025-12-11)—segmentation risk, not a measured €/t delta.

Carbon-Markets/Methodologies/CSI-GPC-vs-.content:
CSI GPC vs SPC Permanence Classes
How CSI Global Biochar C-Sink v3.3 splits soil-applied biochar carbon into geologically persistent (GPC) and semi-persistent (SPC) pools, and how Ro / HyPy unlock the upper class.
Primary: Global Biochar C-Sink 3.3 PDF Ch. 3 · Formulas PDF · science context Permanence Science for Credits.

Definitions (v3.3 glossary)

























TermMeaningGPCFraction expected to persist >1000 years and enter the geological carbon cycleSPCFraction expected to decay within the first 1000 years after soil application (temporary C-sink)CINK_H / C-Sink_HAnnual average mass of biochar carbon stored over horizon H years (t aCO₂e) — integral average of the remaining SPC (and display conventions for GPC)TCETotal Climate Effect — time-integrated radiative forcing (tCO₂e·yr); positive = warming, negative = cooling
Source: v3.3 glossary.
CSI’s framing shift: not “how stable is biochar?” but “what size is the GPC fraction?” once applied to soil (v3.3 §3.2).

Three operative classes (v3.3)





























ClassGate% GPC% SPCSPC-onlyH/C_org > 0.400100Lower persistenceH/C_org ≤ 0.40, upper criteria not met7525Upper persistenceH/C_org ≤ 0.40 and Ro or HyPy gate9010
(v3.3 §1.1, §3.5–3.6; formulas §2.1.2)
Upper-class analytical gates (either suffices)

Mean random reflectance Ro ≥ 3.8%, with:

≤ 3% of measured points with Ro < 2%
≥ 500 measured points
Gaussian distribution
heterogeneity score ≤ 8


BC_HyPy ≥ 90% of total organic carbon (hydropyrolysis-resistant fraction)

Ro resolves microscale heterogeneity / mixed batches; HyPy isolates a condensed-carbon operational fraction. CSI accepts either to keep lab access practical (v3.3 §3.6).
Sampling rule: Ro/HyPy must be on the same representative EBC/WBC batch sample; separate campaigns are rejected. Retroactive Ro/HyPy requires the sample registered in the Global Biochar Tool plus elemental analysis + SEC per EBC Table 1 (v3.3 §3.7).

Worked example (standard Table 2)
100 t biochar DM, 80% C → 80 t C ≈ 293.3 t CO₂e total.









































RowH/C_orgRoGPC (t CO₂e)SPC (t CO₂e)CINK_100 from SPCCO₂-offsettable GPCUpper0.153.90%26429.315.4264Lower0.302.80%22073.338.5220SPC-only0.601.80%0293.3153.90
(v3.3 Table 2). Online SPC calculator referenced on Carbon Standards site from the same table caption.

SPC decay function
From the formulas companion (4000115EN §2.1.2):
[
C_{\mathrm{remain}}(y) = M_{BC}\cdot C_{\mathrm{cont}}\cdot\Big(%GPC + %SPC\cdot\big(0.1787,e^{-0.5337 y} + 0.8237,e^{-0.00997 y}\big)\Big)
]
SPC is described as having a minimum half-life of ~50 years (MRT ~83 years) in the narrative intro (v3.3 §1.1).
Climate-service use of SPC: CINK_H (e.g. CINK_20, CINK_100, CINK_200) for methane compensation and temporary offsetting — transparently distinct from geological CO₂ offsetting, which CSI restricts to the GPC pool (v3.3 §3.4, §3.7). See also CSI MRV and Emission Portfolio for CH₄ TCE matching.

Proxies and science stance






























ProxyRole in CSICaveat in-standardH/C_orgClass gate (0.40); bulk aromatic condensation proxy with longest incubation/field empirical baseAverage property; ash-rich chars can under/over-estimate; mineral-bound H; see Azzi / Lebrun Thauront citations in §3.3RoUpper-class gate (≥3.8%); microscaleNeeds endorsed lab + ≥500 points + distributional QCBC_HyPyAlternate upper-class gate (≥90%)Operational fraction; availability differs by labSoil temperature (Woolf-style)Not used as a global adjustment in v3.3 opsFootnote: lab vs field stabilizing mechanisms; data insufficient for global T effect (v3.3 Ch. 3 footnote)
Literature cited in-standard includes Woolf et al. 2021 (DOI), Sanei et al. 2024 (DOI), Schmidt et al. 2025 (DOI), Azzi et al. 2024 (DOI).
Forward look: v3.3 says classes will be refined in the 2026/27 update; higher GPC for a batch may be adjusted retrospectively under future rules (§3.7). Draft v4.0 existed in consultation (closed 30 Apr 2026) but v3.3 is the live standard (service page).

Materials vs soil

























PathwayPersistence treatment (high level)SourceSoil / geological entryGPC/SPC split by class; SPC decays from year 0Ch. 3, 12.1Composites / plastics (matrix positive list)Entire C persists while the material exists; removed from registry at destruction/disposal§1.1; matrix listConcrete / asphalt / mineral binders100% persistence during structure life; EoL landfill can start soil-like curves after a protected period (concrete narrative: ≥100y protected then curves — see Ch. 12.3–12.4)Ch. 12.3–12.4; §3.7
Matrix positive list header (v4_17, 28 May 2026) restates the same GPC/SPC splits for H/C_org < 0.40 (4000078EN).

Cross-standard comparison (permanence only)






























ProgramHorizon / claimQuantifying gate closest to CSI upper classCSI v3.3GPC >1000y / SPC ≤1000yRo ≥ 3.8% or HyPy ≥ 90% → 90% GPCIsometric200y or 1000yRo ≥ 2% path → 1000y module (protocol)Puro Ed. 2025Several centuries (CORC200+)Ro encouraged, not quantifying (permanence post)Verra VM0044100 yearsH/C_org → Table 3 temperature factors
Chooser: Verra vs Isometric vs Puro · Puro vs Other Standards. Science camps: Permanence Science for Credits.
Practical lab note: CSI’s 3.8% Ro bar is materially stricter than Isometric’s 2% 1000-year threshold — budget petrography early if upper-class GPC is the commercial product.

Carbon-Markets/Methodologies/CSI-Global-.content:
CSI Global Biochar C-Sink
Operator: Carbon Standards International AG (CSI), with science authorship by the Ithaka Institute (formerly framed as “EBC Biochar C-Sink”)
Registry: Global C-Sink Registry
Current industrial standard: Global Biochar C-Sink Standard 3.3 (valid since 9 June 2026); prior v3.2 from 15 November 2025
PDF: 4000039EN.pdf
Formulas & EFs: 4000115EN.pdf
This note is the map of the CSI biochar C-sink cluster. Child notes hold overview history, GPC/SPC permanence, and MRV / emission portfolio. Research dump: /workspace/biochar-research/csi-c-sink-deep-dive.md (2026-09-16).
Cross-standards: Verra vs Isometric vs Puro · Puro vs Other Standards · Verra VM0044 · Isometric Biochar Protocol · Puro.earth Overview · Product Standards EBC IBI

Why it matters for biochar
CSI sits at the intersection of product certification (EBC/WBC) and C-sink accounting. It does not issue a classic multi-sector offset unit; it certifies tracked biochar C-sinks split into:




















PoolMeaning (v3.3)Typical climate useGPCGeologically persistent carbon (>1000 years)CO₂ / N₂O offsetting under CSI logicSPCSemi-persistent carbon (decays over ≤1000 years)Temporary climate services; CH₄ offsetting via TCE
That GPC/SPC split — plus an upper persistence class unlocked by Ro ≥ 3.8% or BC_HyPy ≥ 90% — is CSI’s distinctive permanence story relative to Puro’s CORC200+ centuries claim and Verra’s 100-year Table 3 factors. See CSI GPC vs SPC Permanence Classes · Permanence Science for Credits.
Related: Biochar as Durable CDR · MRV Stack · Carbon Markets Hub · Contaminants and Quality

Cluster map

































NoteRoleCSI Global Biochar C-Sink (this page)Hub / version / what is credited / link mapCSI OverviewCSI org, registry, Artisan, EU CS-BCR, ICVCMCSI GPC vs SPC Permanence ClassesPersistence classes, Ro/HyPy, CINK_H, materialsCSI MRV and Emission PortfolioEmission portfolio, MoS, fossil plan, dMRV, applicationsProduct Standards EBC IBIEBC/WBC prerequisite (Policy)Puro vs Other Standards · Verra vs Isometric vs PuroChoosers

Prerequisite: EBC / WBC
Only EBC- or WBC-certified biochar may receive Global Biochar C-Sink certification. Product class must match use (e.g. EBC-Agro / WBC-Agro for agricultural soil). Persistence analytics beyond the EBC Basic package (Ro, HyPy) must be requested as part of the same EBC/WBC batch analysis — separate sampling is not accepted (v3.3 §1.3).
Deepen: Product Standards EBC IBI · EBC Standard 10.5E PDF · EBC service · WBC service

Persistence classes (v3.3 snapshot)





















ConditionSplitH/C_org > 0.40100% SPC, 0% GPCH/C_org ≤ 0.40 (lower class)75% GPC / 25% SPCUpper class: mean Ro ≥ 3.8% (distributional guards) or BC_HyPy ≥ 90%90% GPC / 10% SPC
Full criteria, example Table 2, SPC decay formula, and materials rules: CSI GPC vs SPC Permanence Classes.

Emission portfolio (snapshot)
All associated GHG from biomass → application must be registered and offset before C-sink validation (v3.3 Ch. 4):

Fossil CO₂ / N₂O → offset with GPC
CH₄ → temporary sinks delivering equal TCE within 5–20 years
Margin of safety 20 kg CO₂e / t biochar (DM), factory gate
Energy-use efficiency >60%; fossil process emissions plan toward <100 kg CO₂e / t biochar by 2030 and <20 kg by 2035 (exec summary wording — see MRV note for §4.5 “biochar-carbon” variant)

Integrity (ICVCM) — research date 2026-09-16

Buyer implication: CCP-methodology-labelled BCR today still clears mainly through Verra VM0044 / Isometric Biochar Protocol until CSI finishes program + category assessment. See Puro vs Other Standards · Risks and Controversies.

When to prefer CSI (compressed)
Prefer CSI when EBC/WBC is already in-stack, GPC/SPC + millennial GPC narrative (or Artisan geography) matters, and/or EU CS-BCR / CRCF is the commercial path. Prefer Verra/Isometric/Puro when CCP method labels, public CORC indexes, or non-EBC MRV cultures dominate. Full chooser: Puro vs Other Standards · Verra vs Isometric vs Puro.

Carbon-Markets/Methodologies/CSI-MRV-and.title: CSI MRV and Emission Portfolio
Carbon-Markets/Methodologies/CSI-MRV-and.content:
CSI MRV and Emission Portfolio
Project-cycle, emission portfolio, offsetting rules, efficiency gates, and post-production dMRV under CSI Global Biochar C-Sink v3.3.
Primary: 4000039EN.pdf Ch. 4–12 · Formulas · service page · vault MRV Stack.

Lifecycle logic (industrial)
EBC/WBC product cert + batch analytics
        ↓
Emission portfolio (biomass → application) + MoS
        ↓
Offset portfolio (GPC for CO₂/N₂O; TCE-matched temporary for CH₄)
        ↓
dMRV track packaging units to eligible matrix / soil
        ↓
Register C-sink in Global C-Sink Registry (after validation)

CSI requires associated emissions offset before the C-sink is validated/usable for compensation (v3.3 Summary & §1.2–1.3, Ch. 4). That is a sharper “pay the footprint first” culture than buffer-pooled VCS issuance.
Prerequisite product layer: Product Standards EBC IBI. Permanence splits: CSI GPC vs SPC Permanence Classes.

What enters the emission portfolio (§4.2)





























BlockContentBiomass provisionProduction, processing, transport (Ch. 5.3 factors / positive list)Biomass storageCh. 6Pyrolysis & site equipmentCh. 7.1 (energy, fuels, CH₄ from unit)Post-production → C-sinkTransport, processing, application (Ch. 10)Margin of safetyFlat 20 kg CO₂e / t biochar DM at producer factory gate
Emissions logged separately as t CO₂, t N₂O, t CH₄. Emission factor = total expenditures / batch dry biochar mass (§4.2).
GWP100 factors (v3.3)

























GasFactorNoteN₂O298Geological offset requiredBiogenic CH₄27.0AR6; was 25 through v3.2Fossil CH₄29.8AR6
Transition: contracts may still use GWP 25 until 1 January 2027 (§4.4).

Offsetting rules (§4.3–4.4)

























EmissionMust be offset withRationale (CSI)Fossil CO₂GPC (geological C-sinks in registry)Long radiative lifetimeN₂OGPCLong residence timeCH₄Temporary C-sink delivering equal TCE within 5 ≤ H_del ≤ 20 yearsMost CH₄ warming is near-term; geological GPC is “neither efficient nor adequate” for CH₄
Self-offsetting with the same batch’s registered sink is allowed once the portfolio is covered (§4.3).
Order-of-magnitude CH₄ math (standard narrative): ~94.6 t CO₂e stored constantly over 20 years offsets 1 t biogenic CH₄; using decaying SPC raises required initial removal to ~122 t CO₂e per t CH₄ (§4.4).
Figure 3 in the standard shows GPC partially retired to cover production fossil CO₂, residual GPC for CINK_1000+ sales, and SPC curve for temporary services.

Margin of safety (§4.7)

20 kg CO₂e / t biochar (DM) ≈ ~0.7% of biochar carbon
Applied at producer factory gate
Not reduced by pro-rata allocation
Covers unquantified Scope 3 (bags, servers, commuting, capital equipment, sampling imprecision, etc.)
Size reviewed at least every two years

(§4.7)

Pro-rata GHG attribution (§4.6)
When biochar is one of several marketable pyrolysis products, facility emissions may be split on an energy (LHV) basis (ISO 14040 framing) if non-biochar products generate income/value ≥ 30% of biochar income.

Feedstock drying heat used for the pyrolyzer itself stays with biochar
Emissions after biochar leaves the unit → 100% to biochar portfolio
Worked Box 6 example: biochar energy share 20.6% of outputs → that share of CO₂/N₂O/CH₄ (excl. MoS mechanics as specified)

(§4.6)

Fossil reduction plan & efficiency gates
Fossil carbon reduction (§4.5 / §1.3)
Producers must maintain an annual fossil emission reduction plan (Global Biochar Tool or upload) covering biomass production → packaging at the facility (biogenic CH₄ from storage/pyrolysis excluded from the fossil plan; transport after gate is trader/processor responsibility).

















DeadlineTarget (exec summary §1.3)2030Fossil emissions < 100 kg CO₂e / t biochar2035< 20 kg CO₂e / t biochar
Wording watch: §4.5 body text says “per ton of biochar-carbon” while §1.3 and the energy chapter cross-ref say “per ton of biochar.” Until CSI clarifies, diligence both; vault default for checklists = exec summary per ton biochar.
Energy-use efficiency (§8.2)
For each certified batch, ≥ 60% of (feedstock LHV energy + process energy expenditures) must appear as used energy / beneficial products (heat, power, biochar LHV, pyro-oil, drying credit, marketed fuels, limited CCU credit, etc.). Failure → batch not C-Sink eligible.
Carbon efficiency (§8.1)
Declared (sequestrable pyrolytic C / feedstock C); no hard threshold yet — transparency / additionality control that pyrolytic use does not replace a more C-efficient baseline.

Feedstock additionality (pointer)
Ch. 5 sets carbon neutrality of biomass, additionality / baseline logic (prefer residues over primary wood that would have been long-lived timber), approved biomasses and default expenditures, and monitoring for perennial systems. Operational detail lives in the PDF + biomass positive lists; do not invent EF tables here — cite v3.3 Ch. 5 and EBC biomass positive list (4000095EN).

Post-production dMRV (Ch. 10–11)





































RequirementDetailTrackingEvery packaging unit labeled (QR); Batch ID, analytics link, production date, CO₂-removal year, owner, departure GPS, DM tons, C content, emission-portfolio linkCustodyScan at destination; online ownership transfer confirmationSoil consentLandowner/tenant agrees soil is entry to geological storage (ToS / invoice OK); landowner need not be C-sink ownerMatrix endIncorporation into approved matrix can end geographic tracking if oxidation loss is precludedToolsCSI-endorsed dMRV providers (4000162EN); may use own QR if linked to Global Biochar Tool batch pageStorage >1 year on siteMay register as temporary C-sink (Ch. 12.6)Processors / tradersMust be EBC/WBC certified as processor and/or trader; footprints enter portfolios
Dry matter: on-site DM protocol per ≤ 10 m³ (or ≤7 big bags): ≥20 subsamples → ≥10 L; dry 110 °C ≥16 h (or endorsed LOD analyzer); round DM % to whole percent; label each unit with dry weight (§9.2).
Geo-localization: GPS in field for defined applications; photo with date/geolocation recommended (Ch. 11). Diffuse C-sinks: Ch. 11.2 + matrix list.

Eligible applications (Ch. 12 snapshot)





























UseKey ruleSoil≥ 50:50 vol mix with soil/amendment (else temporary storage); high root-zone concentration OK if covered in agronomic contextAnimal farmingFeed/bedding/manure additive OK if manure ultimately to soil; exclude energetic manure paths (horse/poultry caution); pet feed generally excludedConcrete / mineral constructionSink while structure exists; EoL landfill / recycle pathways detailed in §12.3Asphalt / composites§12.4–12.5 + matrix positive listOtherOnly forms allowed by matrix positive list / §12.7
Matrix list: 4000078EN.pdf (v4_17, 28 May 2026).

Validation / verification culture






























StepActorNotesProduct certEBC/WBC + endorsed lab + annual on-sitePrerequisiteTechnical / C-sink controlsCSI tools + endorsed dMRVEmission portfolio, efficiency, trackingValidation & verificationEndorsed VVB (CERES-CERT AG highlighted)PDD template on service page; public consultation while Ongoing ValidationIssuance / tradeGlobal C-Sink Registry; endorsed traders for transfer/retirementCSI Overview
Artisan track uses a distinct Manager endorsement → VVB path — CSI Overview.

CSI Overview
Carbon Standards International AG (CSI) is the Swiss standard-setter behind the Global C-Sink family and the EBC / WBC product certificates. For biochar CDR diligence, treat CSI as a product + C-sink stack, not a Nasdaq-style engineered-CDR marketplace like Puro.earth Overview.
Hub method note: CSI Global Biochar C-Sink. Research: /workspace/biochar-research/csi-c-sink-deep-dive.md (2026-09-16).

Organization



































FactDetailSourceLegal entityCarbon Standards International AG, Frick, Switzerlandcarbon-standards.comFounded2021 — joint initiative of EASY-CERT group AG and Ithaka InstituteICVCM applicationScience partnerIthaka Institute (Arbaz / Goldbach); authors of Global Biochar C-Sink include Hans-Peter Schmidt & Nikolas Hagemann (Agroscope affiliation on imprint)v3.3 PDF; ithaka-institut.orgGovernance (application claim)Board: Hans-Peter Schmidt, Ueli Steiner (President), Michael Stelzl; Management Board led by Ueli Steiner (CEO)ICVCM application; team pageRoleStandard-setting + digital tools (Global Biochar Tool) + Global C-Sink Registry; third-party VVB (CERES-CERT AG) auditsservice page
CSI’s ICVCM programme summary positions the organization for nature-based carbon removal standards with “low-barrier access” and scientifically verified sinks (application PDF).

Biochar-relevant standards family
EBC / WBC product certificates  ──prerequisite──►  Global Biochar C-Sink (industrial)
                                                      │

                                                      │

Global C-Sink Registry
All certified biochar C-sinks under the Global Biochar C-Sink standard are registered in the Global C-Sink Registry, owned/run by Carbon Standards (v3.3 §1.2).
Registry holds (per standard): application amount/location, biochar quality, persistence, year of original CO₂ removal, C-sink owner, and the emission portfolio that must be offset before the sink is usable for compensation.

Public consultation of projects appears as status Ongoing Validation (service page)
Transfers and retirements: endorsed C-Sink Traders only (same page)


Global Artisan C-Sink (distributed track)
Separate from the industrial EBC→C-Sink path. Key eligibility claims from CSI (service-505; v2.1A PDF):

























RuleThresholdGeographyWorld Bank low / lower-middle / higher-middle income countriesTechnologyArtisan / Kon-Tiki-type low-tech pyrolysisVolume capsFarmer ≤ 100 m³/year; Artisan Pro ≤ 1500 m³/yearOtherFair compensation / social impact; not dual-certified under other nature-based climate methodologies for the same biomass/SOC story
Process: CSI endorsement of Artisan C-Sink Manager → VVB validation (PDD) → VVB verification (incl. on-site) → registry. Endorsed dMRV providers and labs listed on the service page.

EU CRCF path (CS-BCR)
In addition to Global Biochar C-Sink, CSI publishes CS-BCR (EU Biochar Carbon Removal Standard) for activities as permanent carbon removals under Regulation (EU) 2024/3012 and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/285 (service page; CS-BCR 0.7 PDF; EUR-Lex 2026/285).
CSI states CS-BCR is self-contained: once the Commission approves recognition, compliance with CS-BCR alone is intended to demonstrate Delegated Regulation compliance — aiming for credits comparable to other CRCF units. Public consultation: 26 Aug 2026 – 24 Sep 2026 (service page as of 2026-09-16 research).
Do not conflate live Global Biochar C-Sink 3.3 issuance with unfinished CS-BCR recognition.

Carbon-Markets/Methodologies/Isometric-B.title: Isometric Biochar Protocol
Carbon-Markets/Methodologies/Isometric-B.content:
Isometric Biochar Protocol
Operator: Isometric (registry + Certify platform)
Active biochar protocol: Biochar Production and Storage v1.3 (registry)
What it credits: Ex-post net CO₂e removal = stored − counterfactual − lifecycle emissions
Minimum durability: Project must provide storage > 200 years
This note is the map of the Isometric biochar cluster. Child notes hold permanence math, MRV cycle, and storage modules. Research dump: /workspace/biochar-research/isometric-biochar-deep-dive.md (2026-09-16).
Cross-standards: Verra vs Isometric vs Puro · Puro vs Other Standards · Verra VM0044 · Puro.earth Overview · CSI Global Biochar C-Sink.

Why it matters for biochar
Isometric is a modular CDR program: one production/storage protocol plus specialized soil, low-oxygen burial, and built-environment modules (plus production variants for mobile / distributed / combustion co-product). It is currently the clearest mainstream path to 1000-year biochar claims via random reflectance (R₀) / inertinite science (Sanei et al. 2024), while still offering a 200-year Woolf-style path for projects without petrographic labs.
Registry positioning claim: “largest certifier of carbon removal by contracted volume”; “fully accredited by ICVCM, ICROA, and CORSIA” (protocol page) — treat as operator claims; confirm category-level CCP status separately for diligence.
Related: Biochar as Durable CDR · Permanence Science for Credits · MRV Stack · Carbon Markets Hub · Materials and Built Uses

Cluster map

Protocol architecture
Isometric Standard
        ↓
Biochar Production and Storage v1.3
        ├── Biomass Feedstock Accounting
        ├── GHG Accounting / Energy Use Accounting
        ├── Production modules (mobile / distributed / combustion co-product)
        └── Storage modules
                ├── Soil Environments v1.3  → 200y or 1000y
                ├── Low Oxygen Burial v1.1 → ≥1000y
                └── Built Environment v1.0+ → >1000y

Protocol cites ISO 14064-2:2019 and references ISO 14064-3, 14040/44. Literature review during development explicitly assessed Puro Edition 2025, Verra VM0044 v1.2, and CSI C-Sink standards (protocol Sources).
Minimum review cadence: at least every 2 years or when science/policy changes (protocol Future Versions).

Net CDR equation
[
CO_2e_{Removal,RP} = CO_2e_{Stored,RP} - CO_2e_{Counterfactual,RP} - CO_2e_{Emissions,RP}
]
(protocol §8)





















TermMeaningStoredDurable organic C in biochar × mass × (F_{durable}) (module-specific) × 44.01/12.01CounterfactualBiogenic C that would have remained durable without the project (Feedstock Accounting Module)EmissionsEstablishment + operations + end-of-life allocation + leakage
Issuance is ex-post after durable storage (protocol; science article).

Applicability gates (protocol)
Projects must:

Provide net-negative CO₂e impact per GHG Statement
Meet ESS / no disproportionate harm to underserved communities
Be additional (Isometric Standard; project-specific)
Provide long-duration storage > 200 years

Ownership: single contractual Project Proponent for credits when multi-party supply chains exist — Double Counting and Credit Ownership.

Parent hub: Isometric Biochar Protocol

Isometric splits where biochar is stored into dedicated modules. Production stays under Biochar Production and Storage v1.3; durability and site rules live in the storage module.

Module roster



































ModuleVersion (fetched 2026-09-16)Durability framingURLSoil Environmentsv1.3200y or 1000yregistry.isometric.com/module/biochar-storage-soil-environments/1.3Agricultural Soils (earlier)v1.1Same two-option logicregistry.isometric.com/module/biochar-storage-agricultural-soils/1.1Low Oxygen Burialv1.1≥ 1000yregistry.isometric.com/module/biochar-storage-low-oxygen/1.1Built Environmentv1.0 (page may note newer)> 1000yregistry.isometric.com/module/biochar-storage-built-environment/1.0

Soil Environments v1.3
Eligible land uses
Agricultural soils (FAO cropland / meadows / pasture), forestry soils, amenity/recreational land (parks, golf courses). Other environments (rangeland, horticulture, urban landscapes) possible with prior Isometric approval if risk ≤ agricultural soils and ESS met (soil module).
Ineligible: projects causing sustained net decrease in crop yields / land productivity.
Chemistry & permanence
See Isometric Permanence Pathways 200y and 1000y — H/Corg < 0.5, O/Corg < 0.2, WBC contaminant ceilings, 200y Woolf path or 1000y Ro path.
Safeguards
Application rates within local regulation; minimize dust; incorporate where appropriate; monitor N, pH, salts, WHC, nutrients; heavy-metal remediation plan if soils already elevated; stakeholder process for free distribution (commercial offtake exempt from some consultation rules).
Buffer
Typically 0% (No Observable Risk).
Example
Charm Range & Plains — land application of biochar (registry).

Low Oxygen Burial v1.1
Applicability (strict)

Burial in permitted lined landfill solid-waste sites under local authority
Permit includes EIS if required; ≥ 20 years post-closure care; adaptive management; disturbance safeguards
If Daily Cover: not removed from active area; permanently buried within 1 week
Functional low-oxygen / anoxic storage conditions
Default geography: US, Canada, UK, EU (other jurisdictions if equally rigorous, Isometric-approved)

Future versions may expand to purpose-built burial pits (module).
Quantification
Two Ro-centric frameworks:

Option 1: Ro inertinite fraction plus incubation-derived labile persistence with safety factor 3
Option 2: Ro-only (deducts non-passing fraction entirely)

Site / legal permanence
Hydrology, geology, seismicity target values (module Table 3); base liner & leachate; landfill gas management; oxygen monitoring (report if exceed permit / 5% default); ownership + restrictive covenant/easement + enforcement stakeholder (module Table 4).
Buffer
Typically 0%.
Example + offtake
Carba Burnsville (MN) — woody waste → biochar as landfill daily cover; registry approval 25 Jun 2026; expected first certificates 2026 (registry).
Microsoft agreement: 44,000 credits over 5 years; 1000-year durability via Isometric (Carba press 2025-04-24).

Built Environment v1.0+
Applicable products

Concrete: SCM, filler, admixture, aggregate substitute
Asphalt: aggregate or modifier
Other building materials (bricks, tiles, geopolymers, plasters) case-by-case with similarity proof

Not applicable: carbonate mineralization pathways; lumber storage (module).
Must meet same performance as conventional product; no disproportionate extra installation/maintenance.
Permanence sketch
[
F_{Durable,Material} = F_{Inertinite} + [1 - (3 \times F_{Reversal})] F_{Labile}
]

Inertinite from Ro ≥ 2% + non-reactive C (mean − 1 SD framing)
Default concrete (F_{Reversal}) 2% (PHREEQC worst-case acid weathering) × safety factor 3
Asphalt: labile fraction treated as 100% lost to abrasion over horizon

Storage point for crediting: incorporation into built material. Downstream manufacturing emissions may be excluded if product parity proven; transport exclusion needs national-average distance justification.
Buffer
2% (Very Low Risk).
Development notes
Public consultation feedback from suppliers alterBiota and ecoLocked (Isometric article; Carbon Herald 2025-03-12).
Vault applications: Materials and Built Uses.

Carbon-Markets/Methodologies/Isometric-P.title: Isometric Permanence Pathways 200y and 1000y
Carbon-Markets/Methodologies/Isometric-P.content:
Isometric Permanence Pathways 200y and 1000y
Parent hub: Isometric Biochar Protocol
Modules: Isometric Modules Soil Built Burial
Science: Permanence Science for Credits · Woolf et al. 2021 · Sanei et al. 2024 · Permanence
Compare: Verra VM0044 Permanence and Quantification · Puro CORC200+ · CSI Global Biochar C-Sink
Primary source for soil equations: Biochar Storage in Soil Environments v1.3. Protocol framing: Biochar Production and Storage v1.3. Launch rationale: Isometric science article (2024-10-10).

Two soil crediting options























OptionDurability labelCore inputsConservatism1200 yearsH/Corg + mean annual soil temperature~17th percentile Woolf fit; (F) capped at 0.95; soil T floor 7 °C21,000 yearsRandom reflectance R₀ ≥ 2% on non-reactive CMean − 1 SD on both fractions; (F) capped at 0.95
Stored carbon:
[
CO_2e_{stored} = C_{biochar} \times m_{biochar} \times F_{durable} \times \frac{44.01}{12.01}
]
where (C_{biochar} =) Total C − (C_{inorg}) (only organic C credited).
Projects may combine both tiers under one validation if production batches are temporally and spatially separated with chain-of-custody — each batch under exactly one tier (soil module).

Eligibility chemistry before either option



































ParameterThresholdSourceMolar H/Corg< 0.5Soil module Table 2Molar O/Corg< 0.2Soil module Table 2Heavy metals / PAH / PCDD/F / PCBWBC upper bounds (module tables)Soil moduleLabsISO 17025 or Isometric-agreed equivalentSoil moduleSamplesPrefer ≥ 3 per measured batchProtocol §8.3 / module
Contrast Verra soil gate H:Corg ≤ 0.7 (Verra VM0044 Permanence and Quantification).

Option 1 — 200-year (Woolf-conservative)
[
F_{durable,200} = \min\Bigl(0.95,; 1 - \bigl[c + (a + b \cdot \ln(T_{soil})) \cdot H/C_{org}\bigr]\Bigr)
]





















CoefficientValue(a)-0.383(b)0.350(c)-0.048
Fit uses the 17th percentile of the Woolf et al. (2021) durability distribution (~ one SD below the mean under normality assumptions) (soil module Table 4; Woolf DOI).
Soil temperature rules

Prefer project-specific annual soil T baselining (ISO 4974 or equivalent); ≥ 10 measurements per site-month average narrative in module
Or justified value from global soil T datasets (e.g., Lembrechts et al. 2022)
Air temperature may not proxy soil T (module notes soil often 2–4 °C warmer)
If within-boundary soil T varies by > 1 °C, split project or use highest (most conservative) T

EU alignment note
Isometric’s science article links the 200-year option to the EU Carbon Removal Certification Framework “permanent removal” framing (article). Policy detail: vault EU CRCF references in Carbon Markets Hub / research report — do not invent delegated-act thresholds here.

Option 2 — 1000-year (Ro / inertinite)
Science basis: Sanei et al. 2024 (DOI) — biochars with mean R₀ ≥ 2% structurally akin to inertinite macerals with geological persistence.
Measurement requirements





























RequirementDetailMethodRandom reflectance, e.g. ISO 7404-5:2009Density≥ 500 maceral-level R₀ measurements per sampleReplication≥ 3 samples; submit R₀ histogram at verificationNon-reactive CThermogravimetric residual organic C (Hawk / Rock-Eval-style re-pyrolysis then combustion)Crediting math((\bar{R}{pass} - s{R}) \times (\bar{C}{non\text{-}reactive} - s{C})) then min(0.95, max(0, ·))
Only the fraction passing the 2% benchmark, applied to the non-reactive pool, is credited — reactive C is discounted.
Comparison to CSI upper class
CSI Global Biochar C-Sink upper class uses higher Ro (≥ 3.8%) or HyPy ≥ 90% for 90% GPC — different threshold and pool logic (CSI Global Biochar C-Sink). Isometric’s 2% inertinite benchmark is the Sanei et al. framing, not CSI’s 3.8% upper class.

Buffer philosophy (soil)
Soil module projects are typically No Observable Risk → 0% buffer pool, because labile decay is already discounted in (F_{durable}). Risk reassessed at crediting-period renewal (soil module).
Built-environment module uses a 2% buffer under Very Low Risk framing (Isometric Modules Soil Built Burial).

Non-soil horizons (pointer)




















ModuleHorizonPermanence approachLow-oxygen burial≥ 1000yRo paths ± incubation safety factor 3Built environment> 1000yInertinite + labile × (1 − 3×F_reversal); asphalt labile 100% abraded
Detail: Isometric Modules Soil Built Burial.

Intellectual map across standards




















CampProgramsInputsDecay-model / centuriesIsometric 200y; Puro CORC200+; Verra 100y Table 3H/Corg and/or temperature class, soil TInertinite / Ro millennialIsometric 1000y; CSI upper GPCR₀, HyPy, non-reactive C
Puro explicitly encourages Ro reporting but does not yet quantify with it (Puro CORC200+).

Isometric Project Cycle and MRV
Parent hub: Isometric Biochar Protocol
Permanence: Isometric Permanence Pathways 200y and 1000y
Modules: Isometric Modules Soil Built Burial
